script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

Title: The Secret Recipe

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

Two siblings, JAMES (mid-30s) and ANNA (late 20s), bicker over the dishwasher. They both reach for the handle, their hands brushing against each other.

JAMES
(shouting)
This is my dish! I finished it first!

ANNA
(smirking)
I'll just wash my own then.

James rolls his eyes and exits the kitchen. Anna shakes her head, muttering under her breath.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

James sits on the couch, flipping through job listings online. Anna enters, carrying a stack of cookbooks.

ANNA
(cheerfully)
Hey, James. Have you seen this article about a new bakery opening up in town? They're looking for a pastry chef.

James looks up, uninterested.

JAMES
I don't do pastries, Anna. I'm a savory chef.

ANNA
(sighing)
You know Dad's bakery closed down last year, right? I mean, I love working at the hospital, but we could really use the extra income.

James sighs and stands up.

JAMES
Fine. I'll go in for an interview. But don't get your hopes up. I'm not some sugar-coated pastry chef.

INT. BAKERY - DAY

James enters the bakery for his interview. The owner, MR. WILLIAMS, greets him warmly.

MR. WILLIAMS
(smiling)
Ah, you must be James. I've heard great things about your savory dishes. Now, tell me, what's your secret ingredient?

James looks shocked.

JAMES
(stammering)
Uh, well, it's not really a secret. It's just good-quality ingredients and a lot of hard work.

MR. WILLIAMS
(leaning in)
I see. But what sets you apart from the other applicants? What makes your dishes truly special?

James hesitates, then remembers a conversation with their grandmother.

JAMES
(smiling)
My grandmother used to make the most delicious pastries. She had a secret ingredient that she never shared with anyone. But I think I've figured it out. It's love.

MR. WILLIAMS
(raising an eyebrow)
Love?

JAMES
(nodding)
Yes, love for what you're making and the people you're making it for. That's what makes a dish truly special.

MR. WILLIAMS
(impressed)
Well, James, I think you're the man for the job.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

James works late into the night, experimenting with new pastry recipes. Anna enters, wearing a concerned expression.

ANNA
(worryingly)
James, are you okay? You've been in here for hours.

James turns to her, a smile on his face.

JAMES
I think I've finally figured it out, Anna. The secret ingredient to a great pastry.

ANNA
(intrigued)
What is it?

JAMES
(whispering)
Love.

INT. BAKERY - MORNING

Customers line up outside the bakery, eager to try James' pastries. Anna watches proudly as her brother sells out of everything in record time.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James and Anna sit on the couch, exhausted but happy.

ANNA
(smiling)
I'm glad you took this opportunity, James. We really needed the extra income.

JAMES
(smiling back)
But more than that, I'm glad I was able to find a new passion in something I never thought I'd enjoy. And I know Grandma is proud of us.

They share a look, their bond strengthened by their shared ambition and love for what they do.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
